content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to first use the Darts method to search for an optimal encoder and predictor for the Siamese network. The experimental results demonstrate that searched architectures can outperform previous work.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The first one to use Darts to search for optimal structures for encoder and predictor in Siamese. 
The search space construction covers several heuristics to mitigate the performance collapse. 

Weakness:
1. Introducing the darts with a modified search space to search optimal architectures for the Siamese network is of kindly limited novelty. It is more like one application of darts. 

2. The searched architectures with Res18 and Res50 as backbones are very different.  In all comparison tables, there is no model parameter size information but only top1 accuracy instead. I am curious about the fairness of comparisons if the model with better accuracy has a much larger number of parameters. 

3. “Moreover, the authors of SimSiam (Chen & He, 2021) indicated that insufficient or too many Batch Normalization (BN) layers could cause the model to underperform severely or become unstable. They empirically demonstrate that the optimal setting for SimSiam is to place BNs after every layer except for the predictor’s output layer. Hence, we follow this assertion by adding BNs after every linear and pooling operation except for the predictor’s final layer.”  
It is better to do an ablation study to compare the performance with and without such assertion, to prove that "adding BNs after every linear and pooling operation" is necessary.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The presentation is clear and the details of the experiments are solid.
content.summary_of_the_review: I give a score of 5 due to some points in Weakness.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a neural architecture search (NAS) method, mainly focusing on the siamese network architecture of self-supervised learning (SSL) methods, including SimCLR, SimSiam, and MoCo V2. The authors adopt a DARTS-like method (I don't get what the exact method was used) with the contrastive loss equipped with the l2-normalized MSE loss of each teacher and student branch. Overall search process seems equivalent to that of DARTS, for example, the number of cells, using the softmax for weighting primitive operations, weight summation of the operations, and selecting one or two edges among entire candidates. As a result, DARTS is fundamental and crafted for SSL methods with the ingredients: freezing backbone, BN/ReLU after every layer except for the predictor's final layer, involving max/average pooling into the search space. The authors demonstrate the proposed method on CIFAR-10/100 using ResNet18 and ImageNet using ResNet50 with SimCLR, SimSiam, and MoCo V2 (ImageNet does not have the result for MoCo V2) and further transfer the searched network architecture to Mask-RCNN fine-tuned on COCO 2014.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros)
+ The idea is simple yet interesting
+ The paper is easy to follow

Cons & comments)
- The novelty is limited. The idea of applying NAS on searching SSL backbone looks promising yet covers a narrow scope. Furthermore, in NAS training, the backbone is relayed as frozen and only projection, and predictor MLP modules are searched. The resulting projection and predictor architectures are not that new but with more repeated basic blocks (FC+BN+ReLU) or with a spatial pooling layer.
- How doe data augmentation affect network search? Using strong data augmentations for SimCLR or other SSL methods is a convention, but DARTS usually do not involve them in searching architecture, so I am wondering if there is a conflict between them.
- Lack of experiments. The authors should do more experiments with diverse network architectures with various SSL methods.
- Can the authors apply the proposed method to the ViT backbones?
- What was the exact algorithm (shown in the paper as a DARTS-like method) used in the architecture search?  
- Why does the fluctuation happen for NASiam at earlier epochs in Figure 3?
- NASiam (MoCo V2) on ImageNet is missing in Table 4.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clearly written but the novelty is somewhat limited. Since code is not provided, reproducibility is may not be guaranteed.
content.summary_of_the_review: The idea of searching for new MLP modules at the head of the backbone looks nice, but the novelty is quite limited. In addition, there are insufficient experimental backups to justify the effectiveness of the proposed method, so I cannot vote for this paper to be accepted this round.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the author propose NASiam, which uses NAS to improve the MLP head of contrastive learning architectures. The proposed NASiam achieves decent results on standard benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- NASiam uses NAS to improve the architecture choice of contrastive learning frameworks, which is not well-explored before.
- The authors provide ablation studies to show the importance of pooling layers in the proposed search space.

Weakness:
- The search space is too small. It would be interesting to have some random search results of the proposed search space to see how NAS contributes to the improvement.
- Projector/predictor is only a very small portion of the whole framework. In previous contrastive learning works, some ablation studies show that wider networks tend to improve more on contrastive learning, so it would be more interesting to see whether NAS can be used to integrate the encoder choice of contrastive learning.
- As the authors already notice that different heads could be better for different networks, it is not suitable to directly apply the head searched on CIFAR to ImageNet. Searching on ImageNet with differentiable method should cost similar time as training on ImageNet.
- The improvement is marginal. Training 100 epochs on ImageNet means the networks are very likely not converged yet.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Please refer to the strengths and weaknesses.
content.summary_of_the_review: Unfortunately I would say this work is clearly below the bar of ICLR, in terms of paper writing, technical contribution and experiment design.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an approach that applies NAS to learn the structure of the projector and predictor in popular self-supervised neural networks such as SimSiam or SimSLR. The authors propose a simple search space for the linear layers and compare their method which applies DARTS to optimize for the optimal operations in these layers. The method is applied on top of three algorithms, namely SimSiam, SimCLR, MoCo and results are shown for linear evaluation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
I find the intersection of NAS and SSL really beneficial for the SSL community since I am convinced that the architectures used typically in SSL approaches are not the optimal ones. However, the proposed method by the authors is not novel (DARTS) and the search space is really simple. Unfortunately, I find the contributions coming from this paper marginal and the approach itself does not appear novel and actually a lot of details in Section 3 would be beneficial to the paper. 
The results are also shown only on the linear evaluation settings, while in SSL many other settings on downstream tasks are typically evaluated, as well as on a semi-supervised setting. Moreover, the results on SimSiam for example do not match the original results from the SimSiam paper on CIFAR-10. SimSiam typically performs on a non-contrastive setting. Why didn't the authors evaluate that?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- Clarity: The paper lack a lot of details, in section 3 especially. The algorithm is only referenced in the text but it is not described in details. Moreover, more details on the search space would be useful for the reader.
- Quality: The quality of the paper can be improved if authors would reevaluate the search space they work on and the NAS algorithm used, since DARTS is pretty old by now. The empirical evaluation does not correspond to previous baseline results from literature.
- Novelty: I find the contributions of this paper not enough significant for acceptance.
- Reproducibility: No code provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: This submission seems to have a lot of work to be done still, starting from reassessing the approach proposed for the problem, clarity and empirical evaluations. I recommend rejection.

content.title: NASiam: Efficient Representation Learning using Neural Architecture Search for Siamese Networks
content.TL;DR: A novel method improving Siamese Networks architecture using Neural Architecture Search.
content.abstract: Siamese networks are one of the most trending methods to achieve unsupervised visual representation learning. Meanwhile, Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is becoming increasingly important as a technique to discover efficient deep learning architectures. In this article, we present NASiam, a novel approach that uses for the first time differentiable NAS to improve the Multilayer Perceptron projector and predictor (encoder/predictor pair) architectures inside Siamese networks frameworks while preserving the simplicity of previous baselines. We show that these new architectures allow backbone convolutional models to learn strong representations efficiently. NASiam reaches competitive performance in both small-scale (CIFAR) and large-scale (ImageNet) image classification datasets. We discuss the composition of the NAS-discovered architectures and emit hypotheses on why they manage to prevent collapsing behavior.
